offence_severity: Death caused due to assault with various weapons - Accused-appellants convicted under s. 302/PC and sentenced to life imprisonment
physical_harm: Victim died due to fatal injuries; one eye-witness sustained injuries including a broken left hand
number_of_offences: Multiple offences/counts charged; conviction upheld for some counts
key_evidence_accepted: The Supreme Court accepted the version of the injured eye-witness (PW-5), the mother of the victim, who sustained injuries while trying to save her son, and the medical evidence showing that the injuries caused by the appellants were sufficient to result in the victim's death.
witness_credibility: The court assessed the main witnesses by finding no reason to disbelieve the version of the injured eye-witness (PW-5), mother of the deceased, despite the son of the deceased (PW-11) being an eye-witness whose statement was recorded after 14 days without explanation.
investigation_status: FIR registered, charge sheet filed, trial completed

appeal_history.trial_court: Convicted under Sections 148, 302 read with 149, 452 and 325 read with 149 of IPC
appeal_history.high_court: Confirmed conviction and sentence of appellants under all charges; abated appeal in respect of accused Sadri; set aside conviction of rest of appellants under Section 302 read with 149 of IPC

prosecution_argument: The cows of the deceased had damaged the crops standing in the field of the accused-appellants, resulting in a heated altercation. The accused-appellants and others formed an unlawful assembly, carrying lathis and other weapons, chased the deceased, entered his house, and assaulted him with the said weapons, which ultimately proved fatal.
defence_argument: The appellants pleaded for leniency in sentencing, arguing that the prosecution's case was not established beyond reasonable doubt and that the role of the appellants in causing fatal injuries was not conclusively proven.
legal_principle_applied: The court applied the principle that the prosecution must establish its case beyond reasonable doubt, particularly regarding the role of the appellants in causing fatal injuries.
sentencing_rationale: The final sentence was imposed because the prosecution established its case beyond reasonable doubt, particularly regarding the role of the appellants who caused fatal injuries, and the conviction under Section 302 of the IPC was affirmed.
judicial_mitigating_factors: Taking note of the age of appellant no. 2, he is free to make a representation to the Government for remission.
